 Search "100 Days of Deception" Episode 8: Can a Pawn Ticket Expose Ga-gyeong's Biggest Secret?
 Jon Lui 3 minutes ago 5 min read She stole his wallet. He gave her his trust. And now, they might be falling for each other before either is ready to face the truth.  👀 
 Ga-gyeong and Tae-ung are beginning to trust each other and fall in love, but the pawn ticket could expose the lie that started it all. (tvN) K-drama fans, the relationship between Ga-gyeong and Tae-woong is getting complicated in the best possible way! 
 In the latest episode of 100 Days of Deception , the pawn ticket connected to Ga-gyeong's first encounter with Tae-woong brings their tangled past back into focus. But while this little piece of paper could expose the lie that started their relationship, something else is changing between the two leads: they're beginning to trust each other, open up emotionally, and possibly fall in love. 
 That's what makes this storyline so compelling. Ga-gyeong still has secrets she cannot afford to reveal, while Tae-woong is letting his guard down and trusting someone who has already deceived him. 
 Can their growing feelings survive the truth—or will the secret that brought them together eventually tear them apart? 
 Warning: Episode 8 spoilers ahead! 
 The Pawn Ticket That Could Ruin Everything 
 Remember when Ga-gyeong stole Tae-woong's wallet and denied being the pickpocket he was searching for? 
 That lie has followed them ever since. Now, the pawn ticket connected to the wallet threatens to bring their first encounter back into the spotlight. 
 For Ga-gyeong, the ticket represents a secret that could unravel the identity she's carefully maintained. If Tae-woong starts connecting the dots, he could begin questioning everything he thinks he knows about her. 
 Still from episode 8 of 100 Days of Deception . (tvN) But here's the twist: their relationship isn't where it was when they first met. 
 They're growing closer. They're sharing more of themselves. And Tae-woong is increasingly willing to trust Ga-gyeong, even though he doesn't know the whole truth. 
 The longer their feelings develop, the more complicated that original lie becomes. 
 Because getting caught isn't the only thing Ga-gyeong has to fear anymore. She also risks hurting someone she may genuinely be starting to care about. 
 The Pawn Ticket Means Something Different to Each of Them 
 The ticket isn't just evidence of Ga-gyeong's deception. It is also connected to Tae-woong's search for his adoptive mother, giving the object a deeply personal meaning for him. 
 For Ga-gyeong, it brings back the secret that could expose her. For Tae-woong, it represents hope of finding someone important from his past. 
 Kim You-jung as Lee Ga-gyeong in 100 Days of Deception (tvN) They're looking at the same object from completely different perspectives—and neither has all the answers. 
 That contrast adds another layer to their growing connection. They're starting to understand each other's pain, but they still don't fully understand the secrets shaping their lives. 
 Will that emotional connection help them face the truth together? Or will their hidden histories make it impossible to build something real? 
 They're Falling for Each Other—and That's What Makes This So Dangerous 
 One of the most interesting developments in the latest episode is how much the dynamic between Ga-gyeong and Tae-woong has changed. 
 Their relationship began with suspicion, a stolen wallet, and a lie. Now, they're beginning to let each other in. 
 After sharing painful parts of their pasts, including stories connected to their mothers, the two leads are developing a more personal understanding of each other. Tae-ung's decision to trust Ga-gyeong with the pawn ticket makes that shift especially meaningful. 
 Park Jin-young as Kim Tae-woong in 100 Days of Deception (tvN) He's no longer treating her simply as someone he needs to question. He's giving her a chance to prove herself, even while important pieces of her story remain hidden. 
 And Ga-gyeong is facing her own dilemma. Maintaining her cover means keeping people at a distance, but her growing connection with Tae-ung makes that distance harder to maintain. 
 That's the delicious tension K-drama fans live for:  two people who are beginning to fall for each other while the truth threatens to catch up with them. 
 Their romance isn't developing in a safe, uncomplicated world. It's unfolding amid espionage, conflicting loyalties, and secrets that could change everything. 
 The closer they become, the more they have to lose. 
 Tae-woong Is Choosing to Trust Her. But Does He Really Know Her? 
 Tae-woon's willingness to trust Ga-gyeong is a turning point in their relationship. 
 By returning the pawn ticket and allowing her to hold on to it, he shows that his feelings are beginning to outweigh his suspicion. His decision suggests that he's willing to give her the benefit of the doubt rather than assume the worst. 
 For romance fans, it's a promising sign. Trust is becoming part of their connection, not just attraction or curiosity. 
 Still from episode 7 of 100 Days of Deception. Their feelings for each other are beginning to show! (tvN) But there's a catch. 
 Tae-woong is trusting the person he believes Ga-gyeong to be, without knowing every detail about her identity and mission. That doesn't automatically make his trust misplaced—but it means their relationship is still vulnerable. 
 What happens when he learns that the woman he's falling for has been hiding the truth about their very first encounter? 
 Will he understand why she lied? Will he feel betrayed? Or will the bond they're building give them a reason to work through it? 
 We don't have to know the answer yet to see why this relationship has become so interesting. 
 Three Questions K-Drama Fans Need to Debate 
 1. Are Ga-gyeong and Tae-woong genuinely falling in love? 
 Their growing openness and willingness to trust each other suggest that their connection is becoming deeper than suspicion or attraction. Do you think their feelings are real, or are they both still too guarded to admit what is happening? 
 2. Is Tae-woong right to trust Ga-gyeong when she is still keeping secrets? 
 His decision to give her the pawn ticket shows how far their relationship has come. But is he being emotionally brave—or ignoring warning signs because he's falling for her? 
 3. Will the truth about the stolen wallet bring them closer or break their trust? 
 Their relationship started with a lie, but it is slowly developing into something more sincere. Can that growing bond survive when Tae-woong discovers the full story? 
 The Dojeon Media Verdict: Their Growing Love Could Be Their Greatest Risk 
 The pawn ticket storyline works because it puts two developments side by side: Ga-gyeong's dangerous secret and her growing emotional connection with Tae-woong. 
 They're no longer simply playing a game of suspicion. They're beginning to trust each other, share their vulnerabilities, and develop feelings that neither may have expected. 
 But trust built on incomplete truths is fragile. 
 Tae-woong may be ready to believe in Ga-gyeong, and Ga-gyeong may be finding it increasingly difficult to keep him at a distance. Yet her secrets haven't disappeared, and the danger surrounding their lives hasn't become any less real. 
 The real question isn't just whether a pawn ticket will expose Ga-gyeong. 
 It's whether two people who are starting to fall for each other can survive the truth about how they began. 
 Now it's your turn, K-drama fans! 💬 
 Are you rooting for Ga-gyeong and Tae-woong to fall in love, or are you worried that their relationship is heading toward heartbreak? 
 And be honest: Would you trust someone who lied to you at the very beginning if you were starting to fall for them? 
 Share your theories in the comments. Let's hear what the 100 Days of Deception  fandom thinks!
